real_s1.explanation: The unit responds most to furry animals, mainly dogs (terriers, spaniels, mountain dogs, hounds), with some wolves, cats, meerkats, lesser pandas and guenons. Within a class, its most reliable trait is a preference for the subject facing right (or toward the camera) over facing left. This held strongly on new photos (d +1.05, percentile 100). Similar units share it in part, but it is consistently strong for this unit. The apparent preference for brightly lit subjects did not hold on new photos. Sharpness, cut-off, subject size, tint and position effects are weak or not specific to this unit.

real_s2.explanation: The unit fires most on furry animals, mainly dogs and dog-like mammals such as terriers, spaniels, wolves, the meerkat and the lesser panda, plus a few odd classes like lab coat and sax. Within those classes its clearest pattern is weaker activity when the subject faces left. It is more active when the subject faces right (row 1, percentile 98) or toward or away from the camera (row 2, percentile 94, just below the cutoff). The similar units show the same left-facing suppression, so this is a trait shared by this group of units rather than something particular to this one. The apparent preference for brightly lit subjects (row 7) did not hold on new photos (d -0.00) and was likely noise. The other rows (sharpness, tint, framing, size) are weak and unremarkable for the layer.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to furry, long-haired animals: mostly dogs, plus wolves, Persian cat, lesser panda, meerkat and guenon. Within those classes it is clearly weaker when the subject faces or points left than when it faces right. This held strongly on new photos (percentile 100), and only one similar unit matched it there, so the right-over-left preference is fairly particular to this unit. It is also weaker for left-facing subjects than for subjects facing toward or away from the camera, but that row was not checked on new photos and the similar units share it. The apparent preference for brightly lit subjects did not replicate.
